analysis: Documentation-only PR; no executable code or security controls change. docs/provider/direct-mode.md adds a section (head lines 179-213) documenting an optional NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP hook. It states the hook reuses existing local authentication, body limits, JSON/SSE framing and cancellation scope. It is absent by default, has no production callsite, advertises no new model, and is concurrency-limited (429), bounded for image input, and format-validated by content. The existing local endpoint (loopback bind, bearer token via LocalAuthResponder, no TLS, no rate limiting) is unchanged; those caveats remain at head lines 99-115. docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md only bumps the date and adds a note (head lines 13-15) that Nemotron Super VL has no qualified RAM tier or serving recommendation. The docs explicitly deny production qualification, so there is no overclaim. Related threats: T-050 (inline media plaintext), T-028 (residual GPU data) and T-041 (cache), but the documentation introduces no new behavior. The hook's implementation (NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift) was not supplied. Whether it truly inherits auth, size limits and cancellation, and whether it avoids temp-file plaintext for images, cannot be verified from this PR. That code should be reviewed when it lands or is wired into a production callsite. No threat-model update is needed now. The note is unverified, not a finding.
